sections.overview: A familiar milkweed butterfly, the monarch occurs across the Americas and has also established populations elsewhere.
sections.identification: Adults have orange wings edged in black and marked with white spots; the caterpillar is banded in black, white and yellow.
sections.habitat: Breeding habitat includes places where milkweeds grow; migrating populations also depend on suitable seasonal stopovers and winter sites.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed on milkweeds, while adults visit flowers for nectar.
sections.behavior: The North American migratory population travels between breeding areas and wintering sites in Mexico or coastal California.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on milkweed; the species passes through egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and adult stages.
sections.ecology: Milkweed compounds acquired by caterpillars can deter many vertebrate predators.
sections.conservation: IUCN lists the migratory monarch subspecies as Endangered; this assessment does not automatically apply to every monarch population.
